chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Jamil ibn Salih from al-Fadl ibn Yasar said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I stand in prayer and see the 'adhrah (a type of leather or garment) in front of me in the qiblah.' He said: 'Move away from it as much as you can, and do not pray on the jawadd (coarse leather).'.

key_terms.الْعَذْرَة: A type of leather or garment, often used as a prayer mat or covering.
key_terms.اَلْجَوَادِّ: Coarse or thick leather, often referring to the raw or unprocessed hide.
key_terms.اَلْقِبْلَة: The direction of prayer (towards the Kaaba).

ai.seo_question: What should one do if the 'adhrah is in the way during prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between merely avoiding the 'adhrah (leather of an animal not slaughtered according to Sharia) and the prohibition of praying directly upon the 'jawadd (coarse, thick leather). It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on both the physical purity of the prayer surface and the ritual validity of the place of prostration, ensuring that the worshipper does not stand in a state of ritual impurity or disrespect.
